## C code documentation guidelines

Ulysses uses the [Doxygen][doxygen_website] format for code documentation comments.

As a general rule, all public declarations (structures, functions, enums, etc) in public headers
must be documented. However, documentation in private code is also strongly recommended.

As a summary, you must follow these guidelines:

 - All Doxygen special commands must use `@`
 - Block comment documentation must use the `/** ... */` format
 - Function out parameters must be explicitly labelled using `@param[out]` or `@param[in,out]`
 - Brief documentation after members must use the `///<` format
 - Avoid putting detailed documentation after members, instead, use block comments before the member

[doxygen_website]: https://www.doxygen.nl/

### C function documentation guidelines

For function documentation comments, you must use the `/** ... */` block comment style.

Parameters must be documented in the same order that they appear in the parameter list. For output
parameters, you must specify the direction in the `@param` command (i.e. as `@param[out]` if the
pointed-to data is only written to, or `@param[in,out]` if the function reads and writes to it).
Non-pointer parameters and pointers to const data should not have a direction specified as they are
always `in`. For pointers that are not output parameters, the direction can be omitted and is assumed
to be `in`.

If the function returns a value, you must use the `@return` or `@retval` commands. Use `@retval`
to explicitly document discrete return values (i.e. special set values that can be returned). Use
`@return` for general return values.

Here is an example of a documented function declaration:

```c
/**
 * @brief Copies elements from a source array to a destination array
 *
 * The source and destination arrays must not overlap.
 *
 * @param source Array containing elements to copy
 * @param source_count Number of elements available in source
 * @param[out] destination Output array for the copied source elements
 * @param[in,out] remaining_capacity For input, the available destination capacity in elements.
 *                                   For output, the capacity left after copying.
 *
 * @return Number of elements copied
 * @retval 0 The source was empty or the destination had no available capacity
 */
uint32_t copy_values(const uint8_t *source, uint32_t source_count, uint8_t *destination,
                     uint32_t *remaining_capacity);
```

### C field documentation guidelines

The following is an example of documentation comments for fields of structures, enums, etc:

```c
// The documentation is brief, so can be put in a documentation comment after the members.
struct io_dshot_response {
    uint8_t *response; ///< Out pointer for the response data
    uint32_t *length;  ///< Out pointer for the length of the response data in bytes
    uint32_t capacity; ///< Capacity of the response buffer
};

// The documentation requires a longer explanation that wouldn't fit in a brief comment
// behind the member. So it should be placed in a block comment before the member instead.
enum my_enum {
    /**
     * @brief My enum value 1
     *
     * Here is a detailed description about this enum value.
     */
    MY_ENUM_VALUE_1,
    MY_ENUM_VALUE_2,
};
```
